project_type: Firmware reverse engineering and binary patching project for Ajazz AJ159 APEX gaming mouse
language: Python (tooling), ARM Thumb-2 assembly (firmware binary analysis)
build_system: None (scripts are standalone Python). Binary analysis uses capstone disassembler.
test_framework: No formal tests. Verification is via script execution and binary analysis output.
verification_instructions: 1. Run selftest on debug toolkit. 2. Run analysis scripts and verify output matches expected disassembly. 3. Verify patch binary correctness via disassembly.
setup_instructions: pip install capstone (for disassembly analysis scripts)
environment_constraints: OPEN_INTERNET available. No hardware mouse connected (analysis is offline binary work only). capstone library installed for ARM Thumb disassembly.
contribution_requirements: Update SESSION_LOG.md at end of session. Document findings thoroughly. Do not delete previous session entries.
key_patterns: Firmware binary at firmware_patch/mouse_app_fw.bin (108608 bytes). Memory mapping: address = file_offset + 0x10000. ARM Thumb-2 ISA. MCUboot image with RSA-2048 signature. Existing tools use hidapi for USB HID communication. Scripts are standalone Python3.
directory_structure: firmware_patch/ - binary firmware files, patch scripts, flasher. debug_toolkit/ - USB HID analysis tools. docs/ - technical documentation. Root - context/session files.
